title: The solution team: parts routed in parallel, an auditor before the holdout, the person at every decision
request: Phase 6 (the owner): the solution multi-agents (router, planner, the engine through the validator, critic rounds, compose and programme, the report) on LangGraph, enhancing what exists; capture everything.
plan: A team graph on a project's thread whose nodes call the studio's modules.
Route the parts in parallel with the programme's own router.
An auditor with send-back before the holdout is read.
The person's decisions as pauses; every node a step; the record kept.
The programme journeys through the team.

decisions.decision: The auditor screens each column alone on the fit rows only.
decisions.why: Screening on validation or holdout rows would choose columns by the rows that judge them; a column that alone separates the confirmed cases almost perfectly is usually written after the outcome.

decisions.decision: The auditor never forbids: the person decides through a new person's move, forbid_columns.
decisions.why: A leak is a judgement about when a column is written; the screen is evidence, the person owns the decision, and the validator refuses an agent.

decisions.decision: Every screened column is a feature.leakage_suspect decision, a suspect with the person's answer.
decisions.why: The screens become a student's homework with both answers, and a person who keeps a suspect contradicts the rule: a label.

decisions.decision: The designer takes the team's routes; refresh_plan stays the one place a plan is drawn.
decisions.why: Enhance, never replace: the parallel routes are the same router's answers, so the plan is the one the direct call draws.

decisions.decision: Reading the holdout is an approval; the approval and the run share a node, every other pause its own.
decisions.why: A node re-runs on resume: a run after a later pause would read the holdout twice.

change: dclab_core/auditor.py (dclab-core 0.69.0, AuditVerdict v1, the state field separation); dclab_rnd/studio/leak_audit.py; the graph move forbid_columns; programme.plan_card and refresh_plan(routes=); capture.leak_screened; dclab_rnd/orchestra/solution.py (SolutionTeam, drive); agent orchestra.solution; the programme journeys' --team arm.

findings.defect: A column forbidden as the solution writes it was read by every programme leaf.
findings.scenario: A {column, reason} record in the forbidden list became its text in excluded(), so the column stayed a measure.
findings.cause: str() of each entry.
findings.fix: Read the record's column (committed apart, 52d0016).

findings.defect: The walk ended after the design.
findings.scenario: The fan-out left next at route and the designer set none, so the edge after it ended the walk.
findings.cause: A node that returns no next inherits the last one.
findings.fix: The designer hands back to situate.

findings.defect: The screen's decisions were refused by the ledger.
findings.scenario: Every screened column's record was refused: task 'classification' is not one of its bands.
findings.cause: The state used the family's word, not the ledger's task band.
findings.fix: binary_classification, the ledger's band.

findings.defect: A planted leak named settled_amount never reached the auditor.
findings.scenario: The data card's name rule marked it a leak suspect and kept it out by itself.
findings.cause: The test's leak had a name the card already catches.
findings.fix: The planted leak has a neutral name (basket_total): what the screen exists for.

findings.defect: A second run trusted the first run's audit and approval: a table re-uploaded with a leak was read by the leaves and the holdout opened.
findings.scenario: Run 1 screened clean and the person declined the holdout; the export came back with basket_total; run 2 skipped the audit, asked only the holdout, and two leaves read the leak.
findings.cause: The checkpoint kept the run's booleans (routed, designed, audited, approved); situate trusted them and never looked at the project.
findings.fix: Each step keeps a fingerprint of what it read (the tables, labels, columns kept out, budget): a change makes it old and the team does it again; a new run starts a fresh thread; an open pause is returned.

findings.defect: A person's keep-out was wiped by a routine label upload.
findings.scenario: A suspect kept out, then a fresh label file attached: the column was no longer excluded.
findings.cause: The ban was written into the suggestion, which attach_labels rebuilds and attach_data clears.
findings.fix: The person's bans have their own field (forbidden_by_person), read by excluded(), cleared by no upload.

findings.defect: The person's approval to read the holdout was not the project's approval of the gate.
findings.scenario: With the policy requiring a holdout approval the team's run was refused after the person approved; without it, the read left no approval in the audit trail.
findings.cause: The team took the answer from the pause and ran as an agent without recording the gate.
findings.fix: The person's answer is recorded with approve_gate(holdout, by person); the agent's run uses it.

findings.defect: An error in the audit crashed the graph.
findings.scenario: A table too short for the split raised in the audit; compose's graceful path was never reached.
findings.cause: The audit node caught nothing.
findings.fix: AuditError and ProgrammeError stop the walk with the reason; a refused forbid stops it too.

findings.defect: The round counter counted audits, not send-backs; a restart while a pause waited screened again.
findings.scenario: Three starts while the audit question was open stopped the run without the person answering.
findings.cause: run() started the graph whatever was open; the audit counted itself.
findings.fix: An open pause is returned when started again; the rounds count send-backs.

findings.defect: The programme could run a plan other than the one screened.
findings.scenario: With a router model serving, programme.run routed every part again after the audit and the approval.
findings.cause: run() always redrew the plan from a fresh routing.
findings.fix: run(routes=) and the registry tool's keep_plan: the plan that runs is the one drawn and screened.

findings.defect: The audit's save could revert a table attached during the screen.
findings.scenario: The project read before the screen was saved after it.
findings.cause: No re-read before the write.
findings.fix: The project is read again before the verdict is saved.

findings.defect: A crash after a saved run ended in a misleading stop.
findings.scenario: A resumed compose ran again; the validator refused the second read and the team stopped saying the programme did not run.
findings.cause: compose did not look at what the run had saved.
findings.fix: compose returns to situate when the stored programme already read the holdout on these inputs.

findings.defect: The separation field gave the rule's answer away to a student.
findings.scenario: Only suspects had separation; every 'no' record lacked it.
findings.cause: The screen returned scores for suspects only.
findings.fix: Every screened column's AUC kept in the verdict and recorded.

findings.defect: The whole verdict was not kept permanently.
findings.scenario: The project kept the last 12 verdicts; the steps kept the verdict's word.
findings.cause: A cap and a summary.
findings.fix: Every verdict kept whole in the project and in the audit step's result.

findings.defect: Clean columns were recorded again at every audit.
findings.scenario: The leak test wrote every clean column twice.
findings.cause: Each audit recorded every unflagged column.
findings.fix: Once for each set of inputs.

findings.defect: An audit pass cleared the plan's blockers on the board.
findings.scenario: After the audit the board showed no blocker while a part could not run.
findings.cause: The audit replaced the blockers with the suspects.
findings.fix: The plan's blockers kept, the suspects added.

findings.defect: The related tables' columns are not screened.
findings.scenario: A leak in the accounts table passes the audit.
findings.cause: The screen reads the main table's measures.
findings.fix: Said in every verdict's note and in the status; screening the links leaf's features is left.

findings.defect: Several paths were untested; the parallel and resume tests would pass on a broken implementation.
findings.scenario: A sequential loop passed the parallel test; the resume reused the saver.
findings.cause: Tests counted steps and stayed in one process.
findings.fix: Tests for each path; the fan-out returns one Send a part; a resume in a subprocess; the screen's unit tests.

findings.defect: The builder was not called through the registry.
findings.scenario: The team called programme.run directly.
findings.cause: No registry tool ran a programme.
findings.fix: The tool run_programme (scope project, move run_programme, its guard the validator); the team calls it.

findings.defect: The new tool and move were committed without their refusal case and without the scripted suites run on them.
findings.scenario: check-commit on b327160: test_agents_validator wanted a refusal case for run_programme; test_harness_gate and test_prompt_gate: tools:project and validator:graph changed since HRN-018 and AEV-033.
findings.cause: A tool schema and a graph move are code the suites must see; the package ran its own tests only.
findings.fix: A refusal case (no programme to run) and make agent-eval (AEV-034) and make harness-eval (HRN-019, 17 of 17).

measurements.name: the dev programme journeys through the team (JPR-005)
measurements.gate: the programme journeys' gate (24.8): right on the card, the workflow, the pipeline and the holdout, no move refused, no holdout read twice; the same parts as the direct rules arm (JPR-001)
measurements.result: 6 of 6 right (95% interval 0.61 to 1.0), 0 moves refused, 0 holdouts read twice; every part as the direct path's: card 6/6, workflow 6/6, pipeline 5/5, holdout 5/5; JP-03 dropped its blocked part through the person's question; the routes the direct path draws
measurements.against_gate: Met: the team reaches what the direct calls reach.
limits: Six written people on one replica; the sealed programme journeys (2 of 10 for the rules) are where the capability falls short, which the team does not change by itself.
The auditor raised no suspect on these replicas: the send-back is shown by the planted-leak tests.

outcome: A programme is solved by a team that routes its parts in parallel, audits for leaks before anything is read, and puts every decision to the person, with nothing of the studio rewritten.
lessons: A screen that decides nothing still needs the rows it reads chosen as carefully as a model's: the fit rows only.
When a framework re-runs a node on resume, put a run that must happen once in the node of the pause that allows it.
A checkpoint remembers what a step decided, never what it read: keep a fingerprint of the inputs with every decision a later run may trust.
A person's decision needs its own field: a field another step rebuilds will lose it.
A new tool or move is a change to the agents' world: run the agent eval and the harness eval before committing it.
risks: The screen's bar (0.98) is fixed, not measured: a real signal that clean would be shown as a suspect, and the person decides.
